Key audit matter:
Valuation of financial assets
As disclosed under note 16 (a), financial assets comprise the most significant assets
of the Group.
The financial assets held by the Group are classified into the following categories
as per IAS 39 Financial Instruments; held to maturity instruments, available-for-sale
financial assets, financial assets at fair value through profit or loss and loans and
receivables.
The valuation of some of the financial assets especially, the unquoted securities is
highly subjective due to the lack of observable market prices. As such, the valuation
is conducted using internally developed valuation models.
Additionally, there is significant judgement inherent in assessing the financial assets
for impairment.
How our audit addressed the matter:
Our procedures included the following:
` Understanding the valuation models used by management to value the
different financial assets;
` Reviewing the inputs used by management in their valuation models;
` Ascertaining the reasonableness of the valuation of the financial assets
using readily available market prices and comparable financial assets
information; and
` Reviewing and challenging the judgement made by management on any
impairment provisions for reasonableness and their reflection of any publicly
available information.

Key audit matter:
Recoverability of premium debtors
Premium debtors form a significant proportion of the assets of the Group.
The nature of the insurance industry in Kenya is such that a significant amount of
premium is received through intermediaries (agents/brokers). There are occasional
delays in the remittance of premiums collected by the intermediaries to the insurance
companies.
There is inherent judgement involved in estimating the impairment provision required
for uncollectible debtors.
